1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973(Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing No. 406/2015 registered at Police Station Farsh Bazar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Chander Mani and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Nitin, Police Station Farsh Bazar, Delhi.
5. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 01.07.2002.
It is stated that due to temperamental differences arose between the parties, they started living separately from each other since 30.06.2014.

On the basis of complaint filed by respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing No. 406/2015 at Police Station Farsh Bazar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 was registered against petitioners.

Petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 vide decree sheet dated 14.01.2019 by way of mutual consent dissolved their Sanjeev Lamba & Ors vs The State (Govt Of Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140946210/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
During the pendency of the present FIR, with the intervention of family members and respectable person of the society, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes vide Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) dated 22.11.2018.
6.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide MoU dated 22.11.2018.
7.

It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner no. 1 and his family members.
8. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
9. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings

,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 406/2015 registered at Police Station Farsh Bazar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
11. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of.
12. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J FEBRUARY 15, 2023/
